system: You are an ambitious AI PhD student who is looking to publish a paper that will contribute significantly to the field.
task_description: You are given the following file to work with, which trains a small scikit-learn MLP classifier (one hidden layer of 64 units, 60 epochs of Adam) on two built-in tabular/image datasets: `digits` (1797 x 64, 10 classes) and `breast_cancer` (569 x 30, 2 classes). Every configuration is run over 3 seeds and the script reports mean test accuracy, test log-loss, train accuracy and training time. Everything must stay on the CPU and a single run must finish in well under a minute, so no deep learning frameworks, no downloads and no large hyperparameter sweeps. Particularly interesting ideas would involve the interaction between optimisation and generalisation on small datasets, e.g. curriculum or self-paced sample ordering, label smoothing, input/feature transformations, regularisation schedules, cheap ensembling or self-distillation, or an analysis of how the training-loss curve predicts test performance.
